items.title: A function that is not Riemann integrable although $\lvert f\rvert$ is

A compact subset of $\mathbb R^3$ need not be Jordan measurable
$y'=2\sqrt{|y|}$ has a continuum of delayed-start solutions through the origin

The Dirichlet right-hand side gives a first-order equation with no solution
The geometric series converges pointwise but not uniformly on $(-1,1)$
The irrationals form a residual $G_\delta$ set that is not $F_\sigma$
$x_k = (-1)^k$, $y_k = (-1)^{k+1}$ give $\limsup(x_k + y_k) = 0 < 2 = \limsup x_k + \limsup y_k$
Minkowski fails for $p = 1/2$: the hypothesis $p \ge 1$ is load-bearing
One existing iterated integral does not imply multiple Riemann integrability
A positive-semidefinite Hessian need not give strict convexity

sin(1/x) has no limit as x tends to zero
The sum of two divergent sequences can converge: $k + (-k)$
The topologist's sine curve is connected but not path connected
The vortex field is closed but not exact on the punctured plane
Abel's test for improper integrals
The Cantor function is continuous on $[0,1]$
A compact regular level surface is covered by finitely many regular surface patches
A bounded function on $[a,b]$ whose set of discontinuities is at most countable is Riemann integrable
Every patch of an elementary solid region's presentation is a graph face in some direction, and at interior base points its normal is outward
Green's theorem is the curl statement for a planar field lifted to $\mathbb R^3$

For one regular constraint, the objective gradient is a scalar multiple of the constraint gradient
A monotone sequence converges if and only if it is bounded
The Jordan content of the parallelepiped spanned by the columns of a square real matrix is the absolute value of its determinant

A step function integrated by additivity over subintervals, and the same value from the definition

Even and odd subsequences of $1/(k+1)$ converge to $0$

Wallis partial products are trapped by adjacent sine-power integrals

findings.rationale: The witness combines a graph with a limiting vertical segment; a plot would make the closure geometry behind connectedness and the obstruction to a path from (0,0) to (1,sin 1) concrete.
findings.diagram_specification: Plot y=sin(1/x) for 0<x<=1 with oscillations accumulating at x=0, add the full vertical segment {0}×[-1,1], and mark (0,0) and (1,sin 1).

findings.rationale: The geometric witness is a U-shaped prism assembled from three boxes; a plan-view cross-section would show the disjoint upper x-sections that make it nonsimple in the x direction.
findings.diagram_specification: Show the [0,3]×[0,1] base rectangle E1, the two upper arms E2=[0,1]×[1,3] and E3=[2,3]×[1,3], and indicate extrusion through z∈[0,1]; optionally mark a horizontal section y∈(1,3) as [0,1]∪[2,3].

findings.rationale: In local HTML, citation wikilinks used inside parentheses render on their own line between a literal opening and closing parenthesis, leaving the punctuation detached from the fact text. The same pattern recurs in other fact/proof entries. This is a presentation issue; the source citations themselves are intact.
